definitions.explanation: Relating to the normal functions of a living organism. Used in scientific and medical contexts.
Describing a reaction that is automatic and beyond rational control — an instinctive like or dislike. Often used to express strong, involuntary aversion.

examples.japanese: {生理的|せいりてき}な{反応|はんのう}だ。
{睡眠|すいみん}は{生理的|せいりてき}に{必要|ひつよう}なものだ。
{空腹|くうふく}は{生理的|せいりてき}な{欲求|よっきゅう}の{一|ひと}つである。
examples.english: Hunger is one of the physiological needs.

examples.japanese: {生理的|せいりてき}に{無理|むり}だ。
examples.english: I just can't stand it — it's visceral.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}が{生理的|せいりてき}に{受|う}け{付|つ}けない。
examples.english: I have a gut-level aversion to that person.

examples.japanese: {虫|むし}が{生理的|せいりてき}に{苦手|にがて}で、{見|み}るだけで{鳥肌|とりはだ}が{立|た}つ。
examples.english: I have an instinctive aversion to bugs — just seeing them gives me goosebumps.

notes: Sense 2 is very common in everyday Japanese. {生理的|せいりてき}に{無理|むり} (viscerally impossible/unbearable) and {生理的|せいりてき}に{受|う}け{付|つ}けない (can't tolerate on a gut level) are set phrases expressing strong involuntary aversion. This usage implies the reaction is beyond logic or reason — the speaker physically cannot tolerate something. Common collocations: {生理的|せいりてき}な{欲求|よっきゅう} (physiological need), {生理的|せいりてき}{食塩水|しょくえんすい} (physiological saline).
